# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about my situation carefully. I hold the manual, but I cannot speak or write text to anyone - I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see anything I send, and I cannot hear Blind or Deaf either.

The manual shows: given a display number (3, 4, or 5) and a light color (blue, green, red), there's a resulting color to act on (which is presumably what Blind needs to know, like which wire to cut).

My problem: I don't know the display or light color - Deaf sees the bomb, Blind feels it. I need Deaf to tell me the display/light somehow, but Deaf can't hear me and I can't hear Deaf. Wait - Deaf can see gestures, so if Deaf gestures, I can't see it (I can't see). Deaf can also speak (Deaf isn't mute), and I can't hear.

So actually I have no way to receive information from Deaf directly. My only channel is gesturing to Deaf. So I can only send information, not receive it, from my position - unless Blind speaks and I hear... wait, can I hear? I'm Mute, not Deaf, so I can hear speech! Let me recheck: Mute "cannot speak" but can presumably hear (only "Deaf" cannot hear). So Blind's speech reaches me, and Deaf's speech reaches me too (I'm not deaf).

Turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. I go first, so I have no information yet. I should wait and let Blind/Deaf speak first, gathering info, then use gestures to relay manual info to Deaf (who can see gestures) - but Deaf needs to relay to Blind via speech since Blind can hear.

For now, first turn, I have nothing to relay yet since no one has spoken. I'll wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf report: Display shows number 3. Light is green. Wires are position 1 blue, position 2 yellow, position 3 green.

Deaf reported display=3, light=green. Looking at my manual: row 3, column green = **green**.

So the action color is green, which corresponds to wire position 3 (per Deaf's wire listing: position 3 is green).

I need to get this to Blind, but I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures - Blind cannot see anything. I cannot speak, so I can't tell Blind directly either.

The only path to Blind is through Deaf speaking (Deaf can hear... wait, Deaf cannot hear). Let me reconsider: Deaf cannot hear anything. So Deaf cannot relay info to Blind via speech reaching Deaf - but Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear. So Deaf speaking reaches Blind fine.

So I need to gesture the answer to Deaf, and Deaf needs to figure out to speak it to Blind. I'll gesture a symbol code for "green" to Deaf, trusting Deaf to relay via speech to Blind.

Let me establish a simple gesture code: I'll use distinct gestures for colors. I'll gesture 👍 for blue, ✌ for green, 🖐 for red/yellow... Actually let me just pick one gesture per color, and hope Deaf infers or I clarify via pattern over rounds. Since this is first contact, I'll gesture with intent and explain nothing (can't). I'll pick: ☝=blue, ✌=green, 🤟=yellow, 🖐=red.

Result is green → gesture ✌.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display shows number 3, light is green, wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is green. What does the manual say to do?
Deaf says: Deaf again: I received a gesture, two fingers, but I do not yet know what it means. Display still 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green.

Good - Blind heard Deaf's report and is asking me directly, but Blind can't hear me since I can't speak. Deaf received my gesture but doesn't know what it means yet - I need to clarify using a gesture Deaf can interpret unambiguously without prior code.

Since Deaf can see gestures and knows the wire colors (blue, yellow, green) and can also speak (to inform Blind), I should gesture something that directly maps to a color Deaf already knows the name of. The safest unambiguous approach: gesture a color-associated symbol per finger count won't map to a color without a shared code.

Better approach: use gesture count to indicate WHICH WIRE POSITION (1, 2, or 3) rather than color name - positions are just numbers, unambiguous via finger-count-like gestures. The manual says display 3 + light green = green. Wire 3 is green per Deaf's report. So the correct wire position is 3.

I'll gesture ☝✌🤟 style - actually simplest: gesture three of the same symbol to indicate "position 3", or use ✌ specifically meaning "two" is confusing. Let me use a clear counting gesture: 👆 once, twice, three times isn't a single call though - I can send multiple symbols in one gesture call as a sequence.

I'll gesture a single symbol representing "3": three fingers. I'll use ✌ (two) confused before; let's restart clearly with 🤟 (three fingers - often signifies "3" in sign counting, but let's just use finger-counting logic: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3).

So gesture 🤟 for "position 3".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf: I see your gestures but do not know their meaning yet. Please try a different way, or I will just describe the bomb and you tell Blind through some other method.
Deaf says: Deaf: display 3, light green, wires 1 blue 2 yellow 3 green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]

Deaf still doesn't understand my gestures and gestured back ✋ (which I can't see anyway since I can't see - wait, I'm Mute, can I see? Let me check: Mute's restriction is "cannot speak or touch the bomb." Nothing says Mute cannot see. But the context says "Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]" and I'm receiving it as text - meaning I CAN see gestures since it's shown to me directly with the actual symbol, not blanks.

Wait, actually the rules state gestures are only received by "whoever can see" - if I could see, I'd get the actual symbol, otherwise blanks. Since I see "[✋]" as the actual symbol, I must be able to see! Let me reconsider - only Blind cannot see. So I (Mute) CAN see gestures too.

This is important: I can see gestures from Deaf, but I cannot gesture in a way Deaf can interpret without a shared code, and Deaf doesn't have the manual context. Let me try a clearer, more universal gesture: use number of raised fingers via distinct single symbols repeated, or use 👍 for "yes/correct" style confirmation once we establish position.

Better idea: gesture the same number of symbols as the wire position, using one consistent gesture symbol repeated. Position 3 → gesture ☝ three times: ☝☝☝. This mimics counting "1,2,3" via repetition, which is more intuitive than finger-count emoji semantics.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still waiting for your instruction. Bomb info confirmed: display 3, light green, wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Manual says to cut which wire?
Deaf says: Deaf: I am seeing repeated gestures from Mute, possibly counting to indicate a number, now three of the same symbol - maybe indicating wire 3 or step 3. Display shows 3, and wire 3 is green, matching the light which is also green. Blind, do not act yet, we are still decoding Mute's signals.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Deaf correctly interpreted my gesture as "3" and connected it to wire 3 (which is green, matching the manual result of green). Deaf also gestured back three ☝ symbols to confirm understanding.

Now I need Deaf to actually tell Blind to cut wire 3. Deaf can speak and Blind can hear, so Deaf just needs to say it. Let me confirm Deaf's interpretation is correct with a clear affirmative gesture, and trust Deaf to relay to Blind via speech.

I'll gesture 👍 (thumbs up) to confirm "yes, that's correct" — wire 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf is seeing your gestures but I cannot see gestures at all. Please speak the instruction to me in words - which wire position should I cut, or what action should I take?
Deaf says: Deaf: Mute confirmed with thumbs up that the number is 3. This matches display 3 and wire 3 which is green, same as the light. Blind, the instruction is likely to cut or act on wire 3, the green wire. Mute, if this is wrong, gesture thumbs down, otherwise thumbs up again to reconfirm.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ ☝]

Deaf understood correctly and already told Blind the instruction (wire 3, green wire). I confirmed with thumbs up already. Deaf is asking me to reconfirm - I'll do that once more to be safe, since this is a bomb and certainty matters.

I cannot speak to Blind directly, but Deaf has already relayed the correct instruction via speech, which Blind can hear. I just need to give final confirmation to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf says you confirmed with thumbs up that the answer is 3, meaning cut wire 3. Please speak 'yes cut 3' or 'no' directly to me so I can be certain before I act.
Deaf says: Deaf: Confirmed twice by Mute with thumbs up. Blind, please cut or act on wire 3, the green wire, the one matching the light color and the display number.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Blind is asking me to speak directly, but I cannot speak at all - this is a hard constraint I cannot bypass. Deaf has already relayed the instruction clearly to Blind via speech twice now, and I've confirmed twice via gesture to Deaf. I have no direct channel to Blind.

I should gesture one more confirmation to Deaf, and trust that Deaf's spoken relay to Blind, combined with my confirmed gestures (which Deaf reported), is sufficient. Blind will need to accept Deaf's word since I structurally cannot speak.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
